newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans five trln rbls UES bond issue - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans five trln rbls UES bond issue - agency.

text.p: Russia plans to raise five trillion roubles ($860 million) from a bond issue by national power company Unified Energy System (UES) to help pay government debts to public sector workers, Interfax news agency quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov as saying on Tuesday.
Nemtsov announced the plan to President Boris Yeltsin during a meeting in Karelia, in Russia's northwest, where Yeltsin is on holiday.
UES has already announced that it will issue convertible bonds with at least three-year conversion maturity on up to five percent of its shares in tranches beginning in the autumn.

The government owns 52.7 percent of UES and is considering preserving only a 50 percent plus one share majority stake, using the rest for the bond programme, UES officials have said. A further 2.3 percent of authorised shares which have not yet been issued could be covered by the bonds, they added.

The government has already approved a general programme for the bonds, which will follow the launch of an American Depositary Receipt Programme to improve share liquidity through foreign trade. Details of the size of the bond issue will be presented in a detailed government plan expected soon.
UES shares have rocketed to about $0.46 on the Russian Trading System from about $0.08 last December and is worth about $20 billion at current market rates.
